title.en: Advanced passive: infinitives, gerunds and get
title.es: Pasiva avanzada: infinitivos, gerundios y get

summary.en: The passive can appear in non-finite forms. Use the **passive infinitive** after modals and many verbs (_to be done_, _to have been done_) and the **passive gerund** after prepositions and verbs like _enjoy_, _avoid_ and _hate_ (_being done_, _having been done_): _She expects to be promoted. He hates being interrupted. The file seems to have been deleted._ Verbs with two objects (_give_, _offer_, _send_, _show_, _tell_) have two passives; the person is usually the subject: _I was offered a place._ In informal English, **get + past participle** can replace **be** for things that happen to someone, often by accident or without warning: _He got fired._ Passive forms keep a formal report impersonal and objective, which suits the formal email of Writing part 4.
summary.es: En español lo resolvemos con «se» o con la voz activa: «odio que me interrumpan» es **I hate being interrupted**. Fíjate en to have been + participio para algo anterior. Get + participio es informal y no se usa en informes formales.

form: Passive infinitive: **to be + past participle** (_to be done_); perfect: **to have been + past participle**
Passive gerund: **being + past participle**; perfect: **having been + past participle**
After modals: _The form must be signed._ _The goods may have been damaged._
Two objects: **person + be + past participle + thing** (_I was given a warning._) or **thing + be + past participle + to/for + person**
Get-passive: **get/got + past participle** (_got stolen_, _get promoted_, _get married_)
Get-passive is informal and used for events, not states: _The shop is closed_ (not _gets closed_)

uses.text: **After expect, want, seem, appear** → _The new tunnel is expected to be completed next year._
**After enjoy, avoid, hate, remember, risk** → _I remember being told to wait outside._
**Earlier events** → _The suspect denied having been in the building._ _The painting appears to have been stolen at night._

note.en: The perfect form (to have been / having been) shows the event is earlier than the main verb.
note.es: La forma perfecta indica que el hecho es anterior al verbo principal.

uses.text: **Putting the person first with two objects** → _All the staff were sent a reminder._ (more natural than _A reminder was sent to all the staff_)
**Informal events that happen to us** → _My bike got stolen outside the library._

mistakes.wrong: I don't remember to be told about the change.
mistakes.right: I don't remember being told about the change.

why.en: Remember + gerund refers to a past memory; for a passive, use being + past participle.
why.es: Para un recuerdo del pasado: remember + being + participio.

mistakes.wrong: The report seems to be lost last week.
mistakes.right: The report seems to have been lost last week.

why.en: An earlier event needs the perfect passive infinitive.
why.es: Hecho anterior: to have been lost.

mistakes.wrong: I was got fired after the merger.
mistakes.right: I got fired after the merger.

why.en: Get replaces be in the get-passive. Do not use both.
why.es: Get sustituye a be; no se usan los dos.

mistakes.wrong: She was been promoted last year.

why.en: The past simple passive is was/were + past participle; been only follows have, had or modals (has been promoted).
why.es: Pasiva en pasado simple: was/were + participio. Been solo va tras have/had o un modal.

examples.en: She expects to be promoted before the end of the year.
examples.es: Espera que la asciendan antes de que acabe el año.

examples.en: I hate being interrupted when I'm trying to concentrate.
examples.es: Odio que me interrumpan cuando intento concentrarme.

examples.en: The file seems to have been deleted by mistake.
Having been warned about the weather, they took extra clothes.
The goods may have been damaged during transport.
I was offered a place on the course, but I turned it down.
All the staff were sent a reminder about the new rules.
The suspect denied having been in the building that night.
My bike got stolen outside the library last week.
There is nothing to be gained by arguing with him.
He got fired after the merger, but he found another job quickly.

practice.prompt: She doesn't like ___ what to do by her colleagues.

explanation.en: After like, the passive gerund being + past participle shows she receives the action.

practice.prompt: The documents appear ___ lost during the office move.

explanation.en: An earlier event after appear needs the perfect passive infinitive: to have been lost.

practice.prompt: Last week all the staff ___ a bonus by the director.

explanation.en: With a person as the subject of a two-object verb, use be + given + the thing.

practice.prompt: Careful with that glass or it will ___ broken.

explanation.en: After will, the get-passive uses the base form: will get broken.
